nodes.name: Asha confronts her unanswered messages
nodes.description: In her kitchen, Asha sees missed calls, a billing voicemail, and a social worker text about Marcus's discharge planning.
evidence: the silence of her own kitchen was the first silence she had stood inside in nine days that no one else was waiting at the other end of, and her phone, when she finally set it on the counter and looked at it, had three missed calls from Claire and a voicemail from Bridgepoint's billing office and a text from Marcus's hospital social worker that began with the words discharge planning meeting and asked her to confirm by noon who would be picking him up

nodes.name: Asha hesitates to call Claire
nodes.description: Asha opens Claire's contact and hesitates long enough for the screen to dim, imagining Claire's exhausted home life and deciding not to call.
evidence: Asha picked up the phone and pulled Claire's contact onto the screen, and her thumb hovered there long enough that the screen dimmed once and she had to wake it again. She watched Claire's name brighten and saw the kitchen on the other end of the line before she had pressed anything, two children at a table and a woman who had not slept, and she could not put Marcus through that door in a voice. She tapped back out without dialing

nodes.name: Asha opens social worker thread

evidence: opened the social worker's thread
